titulo: Perfekt 1: the past with haben (regular verbs): When the Partizip II has no «ge-»

aula.titulo: Perfekt 1: the past with haben (regular verbs)
aula.objetivo: Tell what happened using the Perfekt of regular verbs: haben + Partizip II (ge-…-t), including the forms without «ge-» (-ieren, be-, er-, ver-, ent-) and separable verbs.

sessao.titulo: When the Partizip II has no «ge-»

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: look at the sentences. STEP 2: Questions: STEP 3: where are haben and sein in the sentence? And the participle? STEP 4: almost all participles start with ge-. In which sentences is the ge- "hidden"? Where does it show up? STEP 5: in sentences 4 and 5, which verbs take sein? What do aufstehen and kommen have in common? Compare gekocht and getrunken. Which ends in -t and which in -en?

blocos.titulo: Special cases of the regular Partizip II
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: if the stem ends in -t or -d, the participle takes «-et» to stay pronounceable — just like English "waited", "needed": arbeiten → gearbeitet; warten → gewartet. STEP 2: verbs in «-ieren» take NO «ge-»: studieren → studiert; telefonieren → telefoniert; reparieren → repariert. These are mostly borrowed words you'll recognize (studieren, reparieren, informieren). STEP 3: verbs with an INSEPARABLE prefix (be-, ge-, er-, ver-, ent-, emp-, zer-) take NO «ge-» either: besuchen → besucht; bezahlen → bezahlt; verkaufen → verkauft; erklären → erklärt. STEP 4: rule of thumb: if the verb starts with be-, er-, ver-, ent- or ge-, or ends in -ieren, its participle has no «ge-». (The FSI's tip: «ge-» only goes on a verb whose FIRST syllable is stressed.)

erros.motivo: Stem in -t: the participle takes «-et», like "waited".
The prefix be- already takes the place of «ge-».

blocos.enunciado: Say 6 sentences about last week, with one verb from each group: -ieren, be-, ver-, er- and stem in -t.
Write the Partizip II of 8 regular verbs: machen, lernen, spielen, kaufen, kochen, hören, wohnen, tanzen.
